Use it for searches or reading that would fill your context. [can change files; runs to its end] is never handed off. [can change files; may run in the background] is handed off, keeps editing after your turn ends and cannot ask the user: leave its paths alone until it ends.\nAgents:\n- nester [can change files; runs to its end]\n- reader\n- boxed [can change files; runs to its end]\n- isolated [can change files in a git worktree of its own; its changes come back as a branch]\n- finder [can change files; runs to its end]\n- plain [can change files; runs to its end] Sandboxes for sandbox: reader (Reader: writes nothing but scratch); online; isolate; in-place."
  load_tool 673cfc080df0 "Lazy tools (MCP and extension tools only; native tools are always in your tool list) are not in your tool list. With no arguments, list them (name and one-line summary). With names, describe lazy tools: each one's name, id, description and inputSchema. With run and arguments, run one lazy tool by its exact name or mcp:<server>:<tool>; arguments are its arguments as its inputSchema says. With runs, run several lazy tools in one call: a list of {run, arguments}, at most tools.lazy_load_max, run together when none can change state and one after another otherwise; the results come back in the order sent, each under a heading naming its run. A lazy tool is never called by its own name: a direct call is refused. names, run (with arguments) and runs cannot be combined."

With runs, run several lazy tools in one call: a list of {run, arguments}, at most tools.lazy_load_max, run together when none can change state and one after another otherwise; the results come back in the order sent, each under a heading naming its run. A lazy tool is never called by its own name: a direct call is refused. names, run (with arguments) and runs cannot be combined."
